title: Normalized boundary and counit data
statement: Let Ω be an algebraically closed field, N>0 invertible in Ω, and A a finite commutative ring with N=0 in A. Put S=Spec Ω, X=A¹_S, P=P¹_S, i the zero section, k=[1:0], and j=D(x₀)→P, so ji=k. Use the ordinary small-etale A-module categories and the fixed arrows of [def-pur-origin-comparison-arrows]. Then N is invertible on X and P, both point ideals are invertible, and there exist normalized finite-twist pullback transport, the canonical supported-constant exchange isomorphism r:j⁻¹k_*A≅i_*A, and normalized supported Cartier Kummer classes κX and κP [def-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer-boundary]. For their derived arrows bX,bP and actual localized counits e:j_!i_*A→k_*A and ε:j_!L_X[2]→L_P[2], e is invertible and j_!(bX) ≫ ε = e ≫ bP. The hom of r is exactly originRestrictionExchange; neither Chern realization nor compact-source normalization is asserted.

proof.text: Pull back invertibility of N from Ω to S and then X and P. The sections of these smooth relative curves are effective Cartier divisors. Apply normalized Cartier boundary existence and uniqueness to obtain κX and κP; use roots/pure-tensor normalization for the twist transport.

proof.text: The square with top arrow identity on S, vertical arrows i,k and bottom j is Cartesian. Finite base change makes supportedConstantExchange invertible; take its asIso as r. Its definition is exactly originRestrictionExchange (the commutative-square witnesses agree by proof irrelevance). Boundary pullback gives the Ext compatibility with this r and the normalized twist transport.

proof.text: For an exact endofunctor H of an abelian category and a natural transformation H→Id, prove compatibility of all Ext degrees with this transformation. Degree zero is naturality. For degree n+1 embed the target in an injective and dimension-shift across its cokernel exact sequence; use naturality of the short-exact Ext class and the induction hypothesis. Apply this to upperStar followed by open extension and the adjunction counit. Transport the pullback Ext identity from the preceding step using the inverse restriction and twist isomorphisms. Ext.hom and the exact-single and shift comparisons identify this result with the asserted derived counit square.

proof.text: Finite-open comparison in the same square is invertible. In its defining composite the open extension of its auxiliary comparison is invertible, so cancellation shows the counit on k_*A is invertible. Transport along the canonical restriction isomorphism. Exact-single realization preserves isomorphisms, giving d.counit_iso.
